findings.title: MetricsMiddleware shares one mutable instance across all decorated clients
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single MetricsMiddleware once and the middleware func does imw.next = next; return imw. Every decorated client therefore shares the same object and overwrites next. If two clients are decorated, the first client's next is replaced, and concurrent decoration/use races on imw.next. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly allocates a new struct per next; MetricsMiddleware should do the same.

findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences request without nil check
findings.body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics unconditionally read req.PluginContext. LoggerMiddleware in the same chain explicitly guards if req == nil and passes through, so a nil request is expected to be tolerated. With ContextualLoggerMiddleware placed before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares, a nil request panics in instrumentContext before it ever reaches the nil guard.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs by returning a new logger
findings.body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. Code under test now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so logs go to the fresh instance and the original TestLogger records zero calls. Any test asserting on InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs of the injected logger will silently see nothing, hiding regressions.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware drops traceID and plugin fields with no fallback
findings.body: The diff removes explicit pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID from logParams and relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The new instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, never traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext. Plugin Request Completed logs therefore lose trace correlation, and any standalone use of LoggerMiddleware without the outer ContextualLoggerMiddleware loses all plugin context.
